e-fd5d180b3a.text: Requerimento RQS 193/2022 (Sen. Eduardo Girao and seven co-signers) requested the Brazilian Senate special session on ufology, and its justification expressly cites the 2021 'Pentagon' UAP report covering 144 sightings of which only one was explained, plus FY2022 NDAA UAP research funding. The report described is the June 2021 Preliminary Assessment authored by the UAP Task Force and released by ODNI. The session was held in the Senate plenary on 24 June 2022 and ended with ufologists handing Girao the 'Carta de Brasilia' urging a permanent joint civil-military commission.

claimed.text: Jay Stratton is publicly identified as the Task Force's director in 2020 and 2021, including in his own statements; he is said to have worked on AAWSAP before, and has said he has had personal experience with the phenomenon.

Grusch testified that in 2019 the Task Force director tasked him to identify every special access programme relevant to its congressionally mandated mission, and that his requests for the further read-ons were refused; the board infers the director was Stratton.
Science reported that Travis Taylor, of the Huntsville contractor Radiance Technologies, was the Task Force's chief scientist; no government chart naming him has been released.
Karl Nell, the Army's liaison to the Task Force in 2021 and 2022, called Grusch beyond reproach and his account of a decades-long reverse-engineering race fundamentally correct.

Tim Gallaudet says a January 2015 Fleet Forces Command email titled Urgent Safety of Flight Issue carried the GO FAST video, warned of multiple near-midair collisions, and vanished from recipients' accounts the next day, which he concluded meant it had been classified into a special access programme.
A Nimitz-era witness says the 2004 incident was never investigated, no crew were questioned and the tapes were never taken.

contested.text: AARO later assessed GO FAST as an object at about 13,000 feet moving about 45 mph with 60-knot winds, showing no anomalous speed or flight characteristics; the same video was attached to the 2015 fleet safety warning, which AARO's analysis does not address.

The board reads the range fouler set as tracking the existence of a reporting channel rather than the phenomenon, with nearly 40 percent of reports from the year after the Task Force was set up, and sets the Third Fleet dead end beside Gallaudet's deleted email as two traces of suppression at fleet level.

On the board's reading, AOIMSG was a naming exercise with no compulsion authority, and the reappearance of AAWSAP-era personnel at the head of the Task Force shows the 2012 termination was an administrative event rather than the end of the government's interest.

The board infers that the 2021 claim of scarce data survived the 2026 releases only because they were published without coordinates, sensor parameters or altitude, and that the 2020 video release was damage control confined to footage already circulating.

lead.text: The Navy-led UAP Task Force, approved on 4 August 2020, built the dataset behind ODNI's Preliminary Assessment of 25 June 2021, which examined 144 reports from US government sources and could explain only one, as a large deflating balloon. AOIMSG was set up in November 2021, and AARO took over the Task Force's data and materials in 2022.

Was Stratton aware of, or party to, the refusal of Grusch's read-on requests?

record.text: The Preliminary Assessment is a nine-page unclassified report dated 25 June 2021, transmitted while Avril Haines was DNI. Its named contributors run from USD(I&S), DIA, the FBI, NRO, NGA and NSA to the services, Navy/ONI, DARPA, the FAA and NOAA.
Of its 144 reports, 80 involved multiple sensors. It identified one object with high confidence, a large deflating balloon, and left the others unexplained.

In 18 incidents described in 21 reports, observers saw objects that seemed to stay stationary in winds aloft, move against the wind, manoeuvre abruptly or move at considerable speed without discernible propulsion, and in a few cases military aircraft processed radio frequency energy associated with the sightings.

The report names sociocultural stigma and sensor limitations as obstacles to collection, and says the limited amount of high-quality reporting hampers firm conclusions about the nature or intent of UAP. Its date range begins in November 2004, the month of the Nimitz encounter.

ODNI's 2022 annual report adds 247 new reports and 119 found or reported late to the original 144, for 510 in total, and refers readers to a classified version. It records AARO's establishment on 20 July 2022 as the Task Force's successor.

AOIMSG was established by Deputy Secretary Hicks on 23 November 2021, overseen by an executive council co-chaired by USD(I&S) and the Joint Staff's operations director, and superseded by AARO eight months later.

Section 1683 of the FY2022 NDAA required an office to carry out the Task Force's duties, line organisations able to conduct field investigations and to analyse data including through materials testing and medical studies, and a science plan for characteristics exceeding the known state of the art in propulsion, signatures, materials and power generation.
The AARO establishment memorandum ordered the Secretary of the Navy to disestablish the Task Force and transfer its data and materials to AARO.

At the House Intelligence subcommittee hearing of 17 May 2022, chaired by Andre Carson, the witnesses were Under Secretary Ronald Moultrie and Deputy Director of Naval Intelligence Scott Bray. Carson noted that AOIMSG did not yet have a named director, and both witnesses said they were unaware of the Wilson-Davis memo.

The Navy released 72 range fouler reports covering 2004 to 2021 under FOIA on 13 January 2023. The 2004 report describes a smooth white object about 46 feet long and records that reporting terminated at Third Fleet with no process to share it; there are no reports from several multi-year gaps, and nearly 40 percent are from 2021.

USS Kidd's deck logs record drones around the ship from 14 July 2019, and a white light hovered over USS Rafael Peralta's flight deck for more than 90 minutes; the Navy, Coast Guard and FBI investigated and the matter reached the Chief of Naval Operations.
David Grusch's witness title at the July 2023 hearing was former National Reconnaissance Office representative to the UAP Task Force.
Brazil's Senate justified a 2022 special session on the subject by citing the 2021 report's 144 sightings, of which only one was explained.

summary.text: Deputy Secretary of Defense David Norquist approved the Task Force on 4 August 2020 under the Department of the Navy, with the Under Secretary for Intelligence and Security holding cognizance; the Navy announced it on 14 August.

ODNI's Preliminary Assessment answered a requirement in the Senate report accompanying the FY2021 Intelligence Authorization Act. It drew on the Task Force's 144 reports, found unusual flight characteristics in 18 incidents, offered five possible explanatory categories rather than one, and blamed limited, inconsistent data for leaving the rest unexplained.

As Congress was legislating a permanent office, section 1683 of the FY2022 NDAA passed in December 2021, the Department stood up AOIMSG in November 2021; after a House Intelligence subcommittee hearing on 17 May 2022, the AARO memorandum of 15 July 2022 disestablished both the group and the Task Force.
ODNI's 2022 annual report, the first successor product, counted 510 reports as of 30 August 2022.
